quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Do not look ahead. Focus only on your controls.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. When the lead rider puts their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of these features except:

options.text: Meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly around your head. It should have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks does not matter.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When you have a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control. They should hold onto passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should happen?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays straight.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
questions.explanation: During a normal turn, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: How many drinks can affect your ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Apply the brakes harder than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes gently to avoid overworking them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. Plan for more space to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Always press both brakes at the same moment.

questions.question: When should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best during normal riding. However, when going through curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway, riders should switch to a single-file line.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you avoid blind spots, see and be seen better, avoid road hazards, avoid wind blasts, and give you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while riding too fast, your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What should your lane position help you do?

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Travel to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in the blind spots of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your space from other drivers and tells them what you plan to do next.

questions.question: What should you focus on when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but seeing the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds above 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly reduce speed, and move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration is affected by how much you drink, how fast you drink, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, which group formation is best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best during normal group riding. However, when going through curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway, switch to a single-file line.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass hazards more quickly.
You have a narrower view so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to what others do.
You can easily follow the path of the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what others do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver around them.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you usually do when someone tailgates you?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up and put distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up is dangerous because it may encourage them to follow at an even faster speed.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Riders should use single-file formation when riding through curves, taking turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. A staggered formation is used on straightaways.

questions.question: Why is it unsafe to ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly alongside another vehicle can place you in the driver's blind spot. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane without warning. This position also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an obstacle, slow down as much as possible before contact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before impact.
